content: Numerous randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have been conducted to assess the effectiveness of real-time continuous glucose monitoring (rtCGM) across various patient demographics. These studies have demonstrated significant benefits in reducing hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) levels, particularly in individuals undergoing insulin therapy. Additionally, rtCGM has been shown to decrease both the duration and frequency of hypoglycemic episodes. The evidence from these trials highlights the efficacy of rtCGM in both younger and older adult populations. It has been confirmed to improve time in range (TIR), which refers to the proportion of time that blood glucose levels remain within the target range. This improvement in TIR effectively reduces the occurrence of both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, thereby enhancing overall glycemic control.
